QUESTION
--------
For patients receiving nivo/chemo (anti-PD-1 + chemotherapy), what circulating
T cell populations at baseline could serve as associative biomarkers for
1-year overall survival?

ANSWER
------
The baseline circulating T-cell population most strongly and robustly
associated with favorable 1-year overall survival in the nivo/chemo cohort
(anti-PD-1 nivolumab + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, NO CD40 agonist) of the
PRINCE (PICI0002) trial is:

    Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells  (as a fraction of total gd T cells)

Quantitative result (primary nivo/chemo cohort, N=27 with baseline biomarker
+ OS: 14 one-year survivors vs 9 who died within a year):
  * Per-SD hazard ratio (Cox proportional hazards) = 0.361
      (95% CI 0.195-0.668), p = 0.0012, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted
      p = 0.0081.
  * Survival-proportional-hazards assumption satisfied (PH p = 0.84).
  * Median-split Kaplan-Meier logrank p = 0.025 (high gd-Tbet vs low).
  * After adjusting for age and ECOG performance status: HR = 0.343,
      p = 0.0007 (effect strengthens).
  * Independent of the correlated Tbet+ T-cell population (multivariate:
      gd-Tbet+ HR = 0.377, p = 0.0074; Tbet+ T cells HR = 0.913, p = 0.82).

Interpretation: HIGHER baseline Tbet+ gd T cells (a type-1 / IFN-gamma-
programmed, innate-like effector T-cell subset) is associated with a LOWER
hazard of death -> better 1-year survival under anti-PD-1 + chemotherapy.
This is mechanistically consistent with a pre-existing type-1 effector T-cell
program that PD-1 blockade can reactivate.

Secondary (suggestive but NOT FDR-significant / not adjustment-robust, so
reported as weaker candidates only):
  * NKT cells (% of leukocytes): Cox HR = 0.422 (p = 0.026, Cox FDR = 0.090);
      age/ECOG-adjusted HR = 0.249 (p = 0.0047). Higher baseline NKT ->
      better 1-year OS. Co-correlated with Tbet+ TCRgd+ (rho = 0.49).
  * Tbet+ T cells (% of CD3+): logrank p = 0.0115, but age/ECOG-adjusted
      p = 0.088 (not significant) and fully explained by Tbet+ TCRgd+.
  * Ki-67+ T cells: direction opposite (per-SD HR = 1.679, p = 0.11), not
      significant; values (mean 0.93, range 0.68-1.0) are biologically
      implausible for a proliferation marker, so treated as an artifact.
  * HLA-DR+ T cells, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD4 and CD8 T cells: no association
      (all Cox p >= 0.21).

Sensitivity check: in ALL nivolumab recipients (including the full
nivolumab + CD40-agonist combination arm, N=51 with baseline biomarker + OS),
Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells remained the only FDR-significant population
(HR = 0.628, p = 0.0079, Cox FDR = 0.0395), confirming the signal is a
genuine anti-PD-1-associated effect and not an artifact of cohort selection
or of the CD40-agonist arms.

Limitations (this is ASSOCIATIVE only): single center-group trial, small
evaluable N (~27), wide confidence intervals, no external validation; the
available data are population FRACTIONS with no absolute counts, so the
driver (numerator vs denominator) cannot be separated; results may not
generalize beyond PDAC / this regimen; the strong positive correlation among
the type-1 T-cell readouts means they are not independent discoveries.

Net: The best-supported "answer" is the baseline Tbet+ TCRgd+ (type-1
programmed gd) T-cell population. A plausible supplementary theme, with
weaker support, is that a broader baseline IFN-gamma-producing innate
T-cell programme (NKT, Tbet+ T cells) also trends favorably.
grader_notes: The agent performed a thorough analysis with correct data loading and feature selection, and its computed log-rank p-values match the expected significant features, but deviations in measurement-scale filtering, reporting of all significant features, and some methodology/reporting details prevent full marks.

ANSWER — PRINCE trial chemoimmunotherapy biomarkers (DA-9-7)

Question: Do circulating immune-cell frequencies correlate with serum protein levels on-treatment at C2D1?

SHORT ANSWER
No. In the PRINCE (PICI0002) dataset, no circulating immune-cell frequency is significantly correlated with any
on-treatment serum protein at C2D1 after multiple-testing correction.

DETAIL
At C2D1 (cycle 2, day 1), the analyzable joint panel is restricted to 4 CyTOF circulating cell populations
(CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells, Conventional DC, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD4 T cells, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T cells)
and 4 Olink serum proteins (CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-gamma, Soluble PD-1). Correlating cell frequency vs protein at the
patient level (73 patients had both a C2D1 cell measurement and a C2D1 protein measurement; n = 65 per pair for the
B-cell/T-cell populations and n = 73 for Conventional DC), using Spearman's rank correlation across all 16 pairs:

- Strongest pair: CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells vs CXCL9, rho = -0.233, p = 0.062 (nominal only).
- Second: CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells vs CXCL10, rho = -0.222, p = 0.076 (nominal only).
- All other pairs: |rho| <= 0.16, p > 0.19.

After Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, the smallest adjusted p-value is about 0.54 (Bonferroni-adjusted ~0.99-1.00),
so no pair remains significant. Bootstrap/Fisher 95% confidence intervals for the two leading B-cell-chemokine
associations include (or sit immediately at) zero: B cells vs CXCL9 CI = [-0.453, 0.006]; B cells vs CXCL10
CI = [-0.424, -0.000].

Robustness checks all agree with the null:
- Partial correlation controlling for the randomized treatments (APX005M and/or nivolumab): largest = CD4 T cells vs
  Soluble PD-1 (partial rho = 0.257, p = 0.039), but FDR-adjusted p = 0.51; the B-cell-chemokine trends persist but
  stay weak (partial rho = -0.21, -0.21) and non-significant after correction.
- Arm-stratified Spearman (A1/GEM/NP/nivo, B2/GEM/NP/APX005M, C2/GEM/NP/nivo/APX005M): no direction-consistent,
  corrected-significant association; the few nominal per-arm signals (e.g. CD4 T vs IFN-gamma in arm C2, rho = -0.63,
  p = 0.003) are single exploratory cells in a 24-test grid and are inconsistent across arms.
- Change-from-baseline (delta = C2D1 - C1D1) correlation (3 overlapping cell populations x 4 proteins, n = 53):
  largest = CD4 T cells vs IFN-gamma (rho = -0.178, p = 0.20), not significant; no pair survives.

Biological interpretation: the on-treatment circulating cell populations measured at C2D1 are mostly activated T-cell
markers (HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4/CD8), a dendritic-cell compartment (Conventional DC), and a specific B-cell subset
(CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells), whereas the on-treatment serum proteins form an IFN-gamma/chemokine program
(CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-gamma, which are strongly inter-correlated here: CXCL9-CXCL10 rho = 0.77) plus soluble PD-1.
These two compartments are not tightly linked: blood T-cell activation frequency is a compartmental read-out and does
not scale linearly with the systemic cytokine/chemokine burden, and soluble PD-1 is a distinct axis (only weakly
correlated with the IFN-gamma chemokines; e.g. vs CXCL9 rho = 0.40, vs IFN-gamma rho = 0.20). The only coherent
direction is a weak inverse trend between CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B-cell frequency and CXCL9/CXCL10, which is biologically
plausible (this B-cell subset is not an IFN-gamma-producing cell; an inverse relation could reflect divergent
differentiation) but is hypothesis-generating at best and is not statistically robust.

Limitations: only 4 cell populations and 4 proteins were available at C2D1 (the wider panels were measured only at
baseline/C1D15), n ~ 65-73 is small and under-powered to detect modest |rho| < ~0.3 after controlling for 16 tests,
the data are cross-sectional (no causal inference), treatment heterogeneity and compositional (relative-frequency)
structure of CyTOF proportions are not fully modeled, and the CyTOF MSI epitope data are C1D15-only and could not be
used for the C2D1 question.

Conclusion: on-treatment at C2D1, circulating immune-cell frequencies do NOT significantly correlate with serum
protein levels in the PRINCE dataset. The observed inverse B-cell versus CXCL9/CXCL10 trend is a weak,
nominal-only, hypothesis-generating signal that does not survive multiple-testing correction.
grader_notes: The agent performed a careful C2D1 harmonisation and pooled Spearman analysis, but over-included a fourth CyTOF population, did not apply per-arm FDR, and consequently missed the required Arm C2 significant finding; source reliability is strong.
